summary: Gustav Salomon Oppert worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin University of the Arts, the University of Bonn, Leipzig University, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and later held a post at Berlin University of the Arts (~1895–1908).
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He later held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy Claxton worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He founded Sharpham College and served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol's Graduate School of Education (attested 2006).

Religious studies scholar Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Lycée Voltaire, ENIO, University of Paris, Hebrew University, Harvard, and EPHE. A founder of Hebrew University, he held posts there (1978–2009), at the University of Oxford (2009–2013), and Lady Margaret Hall (~2009).

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under multiple teachers including Donald S. Lopez Jr., and became Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering studied at the University of Calcutta and worked in Tibetology. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, where he served as Acting Director (1972) and Director (1974–1998).

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University, as a lecturer at Toyo University, and was appointed professor at the University of Tokyo in 1928.

Gyoei Takahashi works in Buddhist studies. Takahashi has been affiliated with Rissho University as an assistant professor (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2026), and served as a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).
Gyoin Hashimoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1921–1925) and under Join Saeki. He served as chief abbot at Yakushi-ji from 1939 to 1967.

Gyoko Iotani studied at Rissho University and worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor (~1984–1993), professor (~1993–2015), and professor emeritus (~2015), and was a former specially appointed professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyokusen Hosaka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College from ~1950 to 1962.
Gyomay Kubose worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu from ~1928 to 1932.
Gyoon Iotani works in Buddhist studies. Having studied at Waseda University (attested 2015), Iotani held an appointment as deputy director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

Gyoshu Nakajo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Kyu-Eon Jang works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Jang has held posts as an HK research professor at Geumgang University (attested 2015) and as a professor at Peking University.
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934) and held a post at Nyugat.

Gyurme Dorje studied at Edinburgh, George Watson's College, and SOAS under Philip T. Denwood and Tibetan teachers. A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he held SOAS/University of London fellowships (~1991–1996) and served as translator at Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).

György Kara was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University, he held posts at ELTE, HAS, Kőrösi Csoma Society, Hokkaido, and Indiana University.
